prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Phoenix for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” personal injury lawyer for every car-accident case — the right attorney depends on the facts of your case (injury severity, liability disputes, insurance issues, whether you’ll need expert witnesses or a trial, etc.) and on what you value (trial experience, accessibility, size of firm, fees).

What to look for
- Substantial experience handling car-accident claims in Arizona and in Maricopa County courts.  
- Trial experience and a record of jury verdicts (not just settlements), if your case may go to court.  
- Track record of recoveries for clients (settlements/verdicts) in similar cases.  
- Good client reviews and peer ratings (Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, Google).  
- Board or specialty recognition (e.g., Arizona Board of Legal Specialization civil trial certification).  
- Clear contingency-fee arrangement (typical range ~33–40%) and transparent explanation of costs.  
- Good communication: returning calls, explaining strategy, timely updates.  
- Resources to hire accident reconstructionists, medical experts, and handle liens if needed.  
- Clean disciplinary history (check the Arizona State Bar public records).

Where to search and verify
- Arizona State Bar “Find a Lawyer” and disciplinary records.  
- Local attorney directories and reviews (Google, Avvo, Martindale).  
- Recommendations from people you trust and from local support groups or medical providers.  
- Local legal referral services and nonprofits if cost is a concern.

Important practical points
- Arizona’s personal-injury statute of limitations is short (generally 2 years from the accident) — act promptly.  
- Most PI lawyers offer free initial consultations and work on contingency (you pay only if they recover money).  
- Ask about their typical settlement amounts for similar cases and whether they’ll take your case to trial if needed.

If you’d like, I can:
- Find a short list of highly rated Phoenix personal-injury attorneys (with contact info and recent results), or  
- Prepare a tailored list of questions to ask at consultations, or  
- Review details of your accident and suggest what type of lawyer or firm would be best.

Tell me a few quick details (ZIP code or neighborhood, severity of injuries, whether liability is disputed, whether an insurer already made an offer), and I’ll put together a short, local shortlist.
